title: AirAsia Loses Less Money, but Its Recovery Must Wait

source.author: Montira Rungjirajittranon
source.title: AirAsia’s Q3 Shows Why Fernandes Pushed the Comeback to 2028
source.note: Single source. Loss given only as the source's US dollar conversion of the loss attributable to shareholders. The record order for 150 Airbus jets, the RM figures and the Cebu Pacific remark were left out.

figures.text: AirAsia Group third-quarter results posted Monday; smaller loss; higher fares made up for most of the jump in fuel costs
figures.quote: AirAsia Group posted a smaller third-quarter loss on Monday as higher fares made up for most of the jump in fuel costs

figures.text: loss attributable to shareholders RM175 million ($43 million), about a third of the second-quarter loss
figures.quote: posted a loss attributable to shareholders of RM175 million ($43 million) ... That’s about a third of its second-quarter loss.

figures.text: improvement mostly from charging more; jet fuel easing from second-quarter peak; planes stayed nearly as full
figures.quote: Most of the improvement came from charging more ... Planes stayed nearly as full as fares rose sharply

figures.text: revenue fell 11% from a year earlier
figures.quote: Revenue fell 11% from a year earlier to RM4.66 billion

figures.text: CEO Bo Lingam: the worst is behind us
figures.quote: “Our third quarter performance suggests that the worst is behind us,” CEO Bo Lingam said in a statement.

figures.text: smaller airline is expensive to run; spends more to fly each seat than it earns
figures.quote: a smaller low-cost airline is an expensive one to run. It still spends more to fly each seat than it earns from it

figures.text: average fares rose by almost a quarter from a year earlier; share of filled seats barely moved
figures.quote: Average fares rose by almost a quarter from a year earlier, while the share of filled seats barely moved.

figures.text: suspended 76 routes in the third quarter, mostly fuel-heavy international flights to India, China and Australia
figures.quote: The group suspended 76 routes in the third quarter, mostly fuel-heavy international flights to India, China and Australia

figures.text: Malaysia Airlines this month became largest operator between Malaysia and India, first time since 2021; Fernandes dismissed suggestions about internal Malaysia flights
figures.quote: Malaysia Airlines this month overtook the AirAsia group as the largest operator between Malaysia and India for the first time since 2021

figures.text: cut spending on staff, airport charges and leases; fixed costs spread over far fewer seats, so cost per seat rose
figures.quote: its remaining fixed costs were spread over far fewer seats, so the cost of flying each one rose

figures.text: fuel is squeezing regional rival airlines too
figures.quote: Fuel is squeezing AirAsia’s regional rivals too.

figures.text: Fernandes dismissed suggestions that rivals could take the lead for internal Malaysia flights
figures.quote: Fernandes has dismissed suggestions that rivals could take the lead for internal Malaysia flights

figures.text: cut spending on staff, airport charges and leases
figures.quote: AirAsia cut what it spends on staff, airport charges and leases

figures.text: funding is the pressure point; ended June with far less cash than it owed within the year
figures.quote: The pressure point is funding. AirAsia ended June with far less cash than it owed within the year.

figures.text: handing back 25 older, more expensive aircraft this year, most of them early; cuts lease bills, less room to grow
figures.quote: AirAsia is handing back older, more expensive aircraft: 25 of them this year and most of them early. ... That move cuts lease bills

figures.text: about 31% of the 234 aircraft in the main fleet out of service at end of September, mostly scheduled maintenance
figures.quote: About 31% of the 234 aircraft in the group’s main fleet were out of service at the end of September, mostly for scheduled maintenance

figures.text: analysts told Skift: new narrowbody delivery slots scarce until around 2033, could slow the comeback
figures.quote: Handing back jets now could slow AirAsia’s eventual comeback, analysts told Skift this month, because new narrowbody delivery slots are scarce until around 2033.

figures.text: funding is the pressure point; ended June with far less cash than it owed within the year; up to $1 billion debt financing; talks with creditors progressing
figures.quote: It is working on up to $1 billion in debt financing and says talks with creditors are progressing.

figures.text: Fernandes denied reports of a government-backed contingency plan; Malaysia's transport and finance ministries in talks with the airline
figures.quote: he has denied reports of a government-backed contingency plan. Malaysia’s transport and finance ministries remain in talks with the airline.

figures.text: betting on year-end peak; add capacity in fourth quarter, restore some routes; forward bookings in line with last year at elevated yields
figures.quote: management is betting on the year-end peak ... says forward bookings are running in line with last year, at elevated yields

figures.text: presentation called 2026 and 2027 a reset and 2028 the rebuild, when new fuel-efficient jets begin arriving
figures.quote: The Q3 presentation called 2026 and 2027 a “reset” and 2028 the “rebuild,” when new fuel-efficient jets begin arriving.

figures.text: Fernandes warned of more painful decisions on costs
figures.quote: warned of “more painful decisions” on costs

figures.text: if jet fuel eases in 2027 as AirAsia expects, higher fares could start turning into profit
figures.quote: If jet fuel eases as AirAsia expects in 2027, higher fares could start turning into profit across the region.

figures.text: AirAsia has shown it can charge more; not yet shown it can make money at its smaller size; until the $1 billion financing lands, balance sheet decides when comeback starts
figures.quote: AirAsia has shown it can charge more. It hasn't shown it can make money at its new, smaller size.
